# Count occurrences of each constructor
constructor_counts = df['constructor'].value_counts()

# Count occurrences of 'ford' (case-insensitive, but table uses lowercase)
ford_count = constructor_counts[constructor_counts.index.str.contains('ford', case=False, na=False)].sum()
# Count occurrences of 'alfa romeo' (note: in table it's 'alfa romeo' as part of a string)
alfa_romeo_count = constructor_counts[constructor_counts.index.str.contains('alfa romeo', case=False, na=False)].sum()
# Count occurrences of 'matra'
matra_count = constructor_counts[constructor_counts.index.str.contains('matra', case=False, na=False)].sum()

# Check if ford_count is greater than any other constructor's count
max_count_excluding_ford = constructor_counts[~constructor_counts.index.str.contains('ford', case=False, na=False)].max()
ford_is_greatest = ford_count > max_count_excluding_ford

# Check if alfa_romeo_count equals matra_count and both are the smallest among all constructors
min_count = constructor_counts.min()
alfa_and_matra_tie_for_least = (alfa_romeo_count == matra_count) and (alfa_romeo_count == min_count)

# Combine conditions
answer = ford_is_greatest and alfa_and_matra_tie_for_least
